correctness.rationale: Re-audited the narrowed unrestricted theorem. With Z=tr(A*U), central selection leaves only the balanced second and fourth terms, except for Z^4 and its conjugate in dimension four. Schur orthogonality on the symmetric and exterior squares gives E|Z|^4=(S^2+Q)/(n(n+1))+(S^2-Q)/(n(n-1)); the alternating determinant projector gives EZ^4=conjugate(det A) when n=4. Normalizing by (S/(2n))^2 gives the two polynomials. Outside n=4 the two extrema of r are 1/n and 1, with exactly equal singular values and rank one. For n=4, the upper deficit splits into the nonnegative singular-value and phase deficits. For the lower endpoint, the geometric mean of the six pair products is sqrt(product x_i), so 1-r is at least 12 sqrt(product x_i); the lower deficit is at least (2/15)(1-r), vanishing at the minimum only for rank one. The normalized complex matrix sphere is connected, giving every intermediate ratio. The original restricted values were not false: Newton's identity and the stated endpoint examples confirm them. The repair removes the restricted optimization as a separate contribution, retaining only an attributed comparison.
residual_risks: The sampled computations are corroborative only. Trace-zero diagnostics in the unchanged checker do not enlarge the repaired theorem.
